subject: CloudMesh renewal & capacity recalibration — Q1 term/design
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@cloudmesh.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
Cc: CloudMesh Procurement <procurement@cloudmesh.ai>, Amit Shah <amit@edgeops.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: CloudMesh renewal + Q1 capacity planning

Mina —

We're approaching our contract renewal window (early Jan). Traffic for our assistant has ramped faster than expected after the summer product push: Q3 average tokens/day is ~5.1M and Q4 has already averaged 7.9M/day. We expect a 30–45% step-up in Jan when we enable multimodal previews and a second production region.

High level asks:
- Can Redwood propose a conservative capacity plan for Jan–Mar that avoids throttling for the preview rollout?
- What term/discounts make sense if we commit to an increased baseline (roughly x1.5 current run-rate)?
- We need a short ROI recap linking cost delta to latency improvements; procurement will need that for the exec packet.

I've looped in Amit from our infra team — he can share a short perf snippet of tail latency concerns we've seen. Happy to hop on 30–45 minute sync next week.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Ruiz
Head of Product
CloudMesh

[Attachment: CloudMesh_Q3_usage.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@cloudmesh.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CloudMesh renewal + Q1 capacity planning

Thanks Elena — this is timely. Short answers up front, then proposed next steps.

Quick takeaways from the attached Q3 sheet: average sequence length is 120 tokens; ~65% of requests are chat-style (multi-turn). The right sizing leans on two levers: model-mix (smaller decode model for non-critical workloads) and a 1.25–1.5x baseline bump with burst allowance (we typically configure a burst pool for preview windows).

Proposed next steps:
1) Internal sizing + cost delta: Ben will run a dedicated vs hosted comparison and show a 12–18 month TCO and projected unit token cost across model mixes.
2) Performance proof: Karthik to validate tail-latency improvement for the variant we recommend (90th/95th p99 numbers) and call out any re-quantization impact.
3) Commercial: I can sketch a term amendment with a 12-month commitment option + a 9-month stepped discount schedule — that usually balances budget cycles and gives you runway.

If that sounds good, propose a 30-min sync Thursday 12/2 or Friday 12/3. I put an initial slot on your calendar (can reschedule).

Cheers,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive — Strategic Renewals
Redwood Inference

[Attachment referenced: CloudMesh_Q3_usage.xlsx]

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena@cloudmesh.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2027 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CloudMesh renewal + Q1 capacity planning — cost sketch

Mina/Team —

Attached is a short cost model (PDF) that compares:
- Option A: Hosted (pay-as-you-go) with a 20% committed discount for 12 months
- Option B: Dedicated reserved baseline (1.5x current run-rate) + burst pool (30% of baseline) with an enterprise monthly commitment

Key numbers (simplified):
- Current average token cost (hosted): $0.0009/token effective in Q4
- Option A (12 mo commit): $0.00072/token (projected weighted average)
- Option B (Dedicated baseline + burst): $0.00048/token after amortized infra and reserved pricing (but requires 12-mo minimum commitment)

Estimated monthly spend impact for the 1.5x baseline forecast:
- Hosted (Option A): ~$345k/month
- Dedicated (Option B): ~$210k/month + $18k/month for burst credits and ops premium

ROI note: if CloudMesh values a 30–50ms median latency improvement that reduces user churn/increase conversions by even 0.3–0.6% on a $3.2M ARR product slice, the economic delta exceeds the incremental reserved spend within 6–9 months. I'll keep the assumptions tabbed in the PDF.

Attaching capacity-runway-model.pdf — happy to walk through numbers on the call.

Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Renewals Manager
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: capacity-runway-model.pdf (report)]

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@cloudmesh.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
Cc: CloudMesh Procurement <procurement@cloudmesh.ai>, Amit Shah <amit@edgeops.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Dec 2027 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CloudMesh renewal + Q1 capacity planning — cost sketch

Thanks Ben and team — this is helpful and moves us in the right direction. A couple quick clarifications before procurement will greenlight:
- Can you confirm the expected p95/p99 latency numbers you referenced in Option B (dedicated)? We need p99 under 350ms for the multimodal preview gating.
- For the dedicated scenario, can we tier the baseline so the first 6 months are conservative (1.25x) and step to 1.5x after the preview? That helps our finance forecasting.

Procurement also asked for a short amendment draft (commercial summary + term table + cancellation/fallback language) to attach to the packet. If you can send that before EOD Monday we'll route it internally.

Amit — attaching the perf snippets we saw in production last week. Sorry for the noise in the data — the spike around Nov 22 is a synthetic load test.

Elena

[Small perf snippet pasted inline]
Request sample: 9:03:17  p50=120ms p95=280ms p99=410ms (peak);
Request sample: 9:03:46  p50=130ms p95=310ms p99=380ms

[Attachment: CloudMesh_Q3_usage.xlsx referenced; Amit's perf notes attached in-thread]

From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@cloudmesh.ai>, CloudMesh Procurement <procurement@cloudmesh.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Dec 2027 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CloudMesh renewal + Q1 capacity planning — next steps & amendment

Elena / procurement team —

Summary and next steps (action items below). We ran a quick micro-benchmark on the recommended dedicated variant and validated the p95/p99 targets when we enable the larger instance class + persistent KV cache: p95=260–290ms, p99=320–340ms on the preview mix (multi-turn + longs). Karthik and I validated this earlier today.

Commercial / term options I've attached: draft amendment (CloudMesh_renewal_amendment_draft.docx) with both stepped baseline (1.25x for months 1–6, 1.5x months 7–12) and a straight 12-mo baseline option. Key tradeoffs called out in the doc:
- Stepped baseline lowers near-term cash impact and keeps you within forecast corridors
- Straight 12-mo 1.5x baseline yields a lower blended token price and simplifies capacity booking (recommended if you prefer operational simplicity)

Action items:
- Elena/procurement: confirm preferred term structure (stepped vs straight) by Tue 12/7 EOB so we can finalize pricing tables.
- Ben: finalize the dedicated vs hosted TCO appendix and embed the amortized infra schedule.
- Karthik: push the micro-benchmark runbook and tail-latency traces to the shared Drive folder.
- Mina: prepare the DocuSign amendment once terms confirmed and route for signatures.

Links and artifacts:
- Cost model + assumptions: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/4721
- Draft amendment (attached) + drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-cloudmesh-renewal
- DocuSign (placeholder): https://www.docusign.com/transactions/XXXXXXXX-CloudMesh-DEAL-4721

I'll be on standup Monday morning if anyone wants a 15-min pre-submit alignment. Thanks everyone — looking forward to finalizing.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive — Strategic Renewals
Redwood Inference
